podcast: MAD Leaders Podcast: workplace culture, employee health and wellbeing

add2abda5b.q: What does the Keep Britain Working Review identify as the main workplace health challenge in the UK?
add2abda5b.a: Ill health and disability are becoming a bigger part of society due to an aging population and younger people developing mental health issues much earlier. This is leading to a large number of working age people becoming economically inactive. The current system fails because employers and workplaces are not very good at handling ill health and disability, causing people to leave work early instead of finding ways to stay in work.
add2abda5b.e: More employees than ever are off sick. What should employers do? With Sir Charlie Mayfield
add2abda5b.rq: We're trying to re-humanize the workplace. We've become very procedural and risk aware, but that can mean lack of contact and relationship between people, which if well supported could help thousands remain in work.

fd25485bde.q: What are the return-to-work statistics for employees absent from work due to health reasons according to the Keep Britain Working Review?
fd25485bde.a: If someone is away from work for 46 weeks, 96% return to work. Once absence reaches a year, less than 50% return. For people who become economically inactive for health reasons, there is only about a 3.8% chance of returning to work within the next year.

12493033ea.q: What is the potential economic benefit of improving workforce participation for people with health conditions or disabilities in the UK?
12493033ea.a: If the UK achieved the same level of participation as some G20 competitors, there would be approximately one million more people working. Even improving the participation rate by one percentage point would add 300,000 people to the workforce, equivalent to the size of Cardiff. This represents an opportunity running into billions of pounds annually in overall economic benefit.

a0da9d613d.q: What is the proposed workplace health system model and what are its key components?
a0da9d613d.a: The workplace health system is founded on shared responsibility between employers, employees, and government. Key components include: employers being actively engaged and on the pitch; developing return-to-work and stay-in-work plans; providing case managers to support difficult conversations; and enabling rapid access to early-stage treatment such as physiotherapy within a week or talking therapies for mental health issues.
